text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today to $150.80, capping a remarkable two-week rally of 12.45%. The immediate catalyst is escalating Middle East tension: Saudi Arabia intercepted Iranian-backed Houthi missiles and drones, while Brent crude oil has climbed to $116 per barrel—a six-month high—as geopolitical risk premiums pile on. As a major oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices rise, and the company has been riding this wave as investors rotate into energy stocks expecting further supply disruptions.

The broader context amplifies the move: U.S. officials have signaled potential military action against Iran, and analysts are now explicitly highlighting energy stocks as a hedge on escalating regional conflict. With world oil prices near $115 and the Iran situation described as "transforming global energy markets" in the companies' favor, the stock's 12% surge over two weeks reflects investor positioning for a sustained period of higher oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty.
